official.application_cycle: Annual, run by each educational institution; award periods are 12 months (April to the following March) or 6 months (October to the following March).

official.application_route: Ask your enrolled institution to nominate you; there is no direct application to JASSO.

official.international_eligibility: Explicitly for privately-financed international students facing financial difficulties.
official.duration: 12 months (April to the following March) or 6 months (October to the following March)
official.description: The JASSO Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students is a stipend for privately-financed international students with excellent academic and character records who face financial difficulties. Each educational institution nominates candidates to JASSO, and the number of candidates depends on the institution's international enrolment.
official.program_type: Privately-financed student honors scholarship (nominated by the host institution)
official.english_requirement: JLPT N2 or above, or EJU Japanese 200 points or more, or a language level separately recognised by JASSO, or CEFR B2 or above in English. The language condition is waived for candidates in preparatory Japanese language programmes, university preparatory courses and Japanese language institutes.

Whether a specific institution will nominate in the current cycle
verification.notes: JASSO's official scholarship page was fetched on 2026-10-10: stipend levels (JPY 48,000 graduate/undergraduate, JPY 30,000 language institutes), 12/6-month periods, the institution-nomination rule, the full eligibility conditions including the JPY 90,000 allowance cap and JPY 5,000,000 supporter income limit, and the language conditions were read directly from the page.

applicant_utility.summary: The Honors Scholarship is a monthly stipend of JPY 48,000 for privately-financed students in Japan with top grades and demonstrated financial need - helpful with rent and food, but it pays no tuition and no flights. Everything depends on your school: it nominates you, and schools with few international students may have no nominations to give at all. Grades and monthly reporting discipline matter more here than any essay, since grantees must sign the designated sheet at the international students' office every month.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Privately-financed students with strong grades and tight finances whose institution runs an internal nomination for this scholarship.
application_readiness_checklist: Ask your institution's international students office whether it nominates students for the Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship this year
Check the means test before applying: your average private allowance, excluding enrolment and tuition fees, must not exceed JPY 90,000 per month
If a financial supporter lives in Japan, confirm their annual income is under JPY 5,000,000
Hold evidence of Japanese or English proficiency ready (JLPT N2+, EJU Japanese 200+, JASSO-recognised level, or CEFR B2+), unless you are in a preparatory or language-institute programme
Confirm you are not holding a MEXT or foreign-government scholarship and not receiving JASSO Student Exchange Support Program support
common_rejection_risks: Your institution does not nominate, which no applicant can override
Exceeding the JPY 90,000 monthly private allowance average
Grades below the grading criteria in the application guidelines
Holding another scholarship that cannot be combined with this one
Falling behind on the monthly signature sheet after the award
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition, admission fees, flights, insurance and most living costs; the stipend is JPY 48,000 per month (JPY 30,000 at language institutes) for a maximum of 12 months.
document_audit: Evidence must show full-time enrolment in the eligible institution type, since research students, trainees, auditors and non-degree students are excluded
The language condition is waived only for preparatory Japanese language programmes, university preparatory courses and Japanese language institutes
The award requires ongoing attendance confirmation, so keep your enrolment records clean
alerts: Selection quota scales with each institution's international enrolment, so identical applicants can face different odds at different schools
After award you must agree to cooperate with JASSO's career path survey
The award runs at most 12 months (April entry) or 6 months (October entry) with no promise of renewal in the same form
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Approach your enrolled institution, submit through its internal nomination process, and if selected, sign monthly at the international students' office for the award period.

official.deadline_note: FY2027 runs two open-call rounds: 1st round applications had to reach JSPS by August 28, 2026 (5 p.m. JST) with results in late December 2026; 2nd round applications must reach JSPS by April 23, 2027 (5 p.m. JST) with results in early August 2027. Applications are submitted by the host institution to JSPS.
official.application_cycle: FY2027, two annual open-call rounds; arrival windows 1 April - 30 September 2027 (1st round) and 1 September - 30 November 2027 (2nd round); 120 fellowships in each round.
official.status_note: The FY2027 2nd round is the next applicable round as of 2026-10-10; the application deadline is 23 April 2027, 5 p.m. JST, with results published in early August 2027.
benefits: Maintenance allowance of JPY 362,000 per month
Round-trip air ticket (based on JSPS's regulations)
Host researchers may apply for a Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research (Grant-in-Aid for JSPS Research Fellow) to cover cooperative research expenses

As of 1 April of the fellowship's fiscal year, obtained a doctoral degree within six years of the date the fellowship goes into effect, or expected to receive a Ph.D. by the fellowship start date
Not a Japanese citizen or a foreigner permitted permanent residence in Japan
Not previously awarded and started a fellowship under the JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship Program (Standard or Pathway to University positions in Japan)
Must be hosted by an eligible Japanese researcher who applies on the candidate's behalf
requirements: A Japanese host researcher must submit the application through the JSPS Electronic Application System; candidates cannot apply directly
Applications must reach JSPS by 5 p.m. JST on the round's deadline date
The fellowship is provided in full month units
Air tickets must be booked through the travel agency designated by JSPS, not bought independently
Selected fellows must submit the doctoral degree certificate or diploma before the fellowship starting date
documents: Application submitted via the JSPS Electronic Application System by the host researcher
Doctoral degree certificate or documentation confirming the expected date of the doctoral degree (required before the start date, not at application)
Research plan and CV as specified in the application call
Documents from the host institution required by the JSPS application call
selection_criteria: Open Call: applications from heads of Japanese universities or research institutions wishing to invite foreign researchers, followed by selection to designate Fellows
Nomination channel: Fellows designated through recommendations from overseas nominating authorities
Each host researcher can submit up to three applications; where several candidates apply at the same time, priorities should be given
coverage: Maintenance allowance of JPY 362,000 per month
Round-trip air ticket based on JSPS regulations
Settling-in allowance of JPY 200,000 and overseas travel insurance
For candidates already living in Japan with a mailing address before the start date, the outbound airfare and settling-in allowance are not paid
application_method: Open Call (Standard): the host researcher submits the nomination through the JSPS Electronic Application System before the round deadline
Invitation route: an overseas nominating authority may nominate a candidate
official.application_route: A Japanese host researcher applies for you through the JSPS Electronic Application System; candidates never submit their own applications.
official.citizenship_residency: Citizens of countries with diplomatic relations with Japan are eligible; Japanese citizens and foreigners with permanent residence in Japan are not eligible.
official.international_eligibility: Explicitly a fellowship for overseas researchers hosted by Japanese institutions.
official.research_requirement: Cooperative research with a Japanese host researcher is the core of the fellowship; the application call specifies the research plan and CV requirements.
official.duration: 12 to 24 months, provided in full month units
official.description: The JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan (Standard) provide an opportunity for young overseas researchers to conduct collaborative research under the guidance of their hosts in universities and other research institutions in Japan, in all fields of the humanities, social sciences and natural sciences.

not_confirmed: English or Japanese language requirement (JSPS publishes none for this fellowship; host institutions set their own)
Grant-in-Aid amounts for cooperative research expenses (application-based, not published here)
verification.notes: JSPS's official About-the-Program and Application Schedule pages were fetched on 2026-10-10: maintenance allowance JPY 362,000/month, settling-in allowance JPY 200,000, round-trip air ticket and overseas travel insurance, 12-24 month duration, eligibility rules, host-applicant rules, and the FY2027 deadline calendar (28 August 2026 and 23 April 2027, 120 fellowships each) were read directly from the pages.

applicant_utility.summary: JSPS pays postdoctoral researchers JPY 362,000 a month plus a JPY 200,000 settling-in allowance, round-trip airfare and overseas travel insurance for 12-24 months of cooperative research at a Japanese institution. You cannot apply yourself - a Japanese host researcher submits the nomination through the JSPS Electronic Application System, so securing a willing host is the real application. Timing is unforgiving: the FY2027 1st round closed on 28 August 2026, so the next applicable round reaches JSPS by 5 p.m. JST on 23 April 2027, and applications are treated in whole-month blocks.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent PhDs (degree within the last six years) from countries with diplomatic relations with Japan who can secure a Japanese host researcher before the round deadline.
application_readiness_checklist: Find and confirm a Japanese host researcher at an eligible institution who is willing to submit the application on your behalf
Check your PhD date against the six-year window measured from 1 April of the fellowship's fiscal year
Make sure the host submits through the JSPS Electronic Application System before 5 p.m. JST on the round deadline
Ask the host whether they will also apply for the Grant-in-Aid for JSPS Research Fellow to cover cooperative research expenses
Have the doctoral degree certificate or diploma ready to submit before the fellowship start date if selected
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 5 p.m. JST cut-off; late submissions are not considered
The six-year PhD clock excluding you, especially if you have had career breaks
A host who is not a full-time researcher at an eligible institution, or who wants to nominate more than three candidates
Assuming a previous JSPS Standard fellowship holder can reapply; they cannot
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The fellowship covers maintenance, airfare, settling-in and insurance only; there is no tuition or fee coverage, so grantees fund their own research-related and personal costs beyond the allowance.
document_audit: If you are already living in Japan with a mailing address before the start date, the outbound airfare and settling-in allowance are not paid - plan accordingly
Air travel must be booked through the agency designated by JSPS; independently bought tickets are not covered
The doctoral degree certificate is required before the start date, not at application, but selection can fall through if it is not produced
alerts: Each host researcher may submit up to three applications, and the host's own priorities determine which candidate goes forward when several apply together
The fellowship is paid in whole-month units, so partial months are not funded
Results for the FY2027 2nd round are published in early August 2027, close to the September-November arrival window - do not commit to other positions until the award letter arrives
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Secure a Japanese host, let the host submit your nomination through the JSPS Electronic Application System by 5 p.m. JST on the round deadline, then await the result and produce the degree certificate before starting.
